subject: Coordination: breach cooperation, timelines & subprocessor visibility
messages:
From: Finex Security <security@finex.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:15:00Z
Subject: Potential data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence access

Hi Markus,

We detected anomalous activity that may have included customer identifiers from our integration with Redwood. We're still triaging but wanted to surface this early and understand contractual obligations and practical handoffs. Specifically:

- What notification windows do you commit to under your DPA when we report a suspected exposure (initial detection vs confirmed breach)?
- Can you enumerate subprocessors that could have had access to the affected data and whether any are cross-border (EU/US)?
- What is your mechanism for secure evidence transfer (forensic logs, container images)? Is there a preferred SFTP/secure share or an escrow process?

I've attached a short incident intake template to capture the scope we have so far. Please let us know next steps — we need an initial operational contact and an estimated timeline for an initial written response.

Thanks,
Aishwarya Patel
Head of Security Operations, Finex Technologies
security@finex.com
Attachment: finex_initial_report_template.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Finex Security <security@finex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence access

Hi Aishwarya — thanks for the heads-up and for the template. Sorry to hear you're dealing with this. Looping in Legal, Ops, and CS so we can coordinate. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Initial commitments (we'll confirm after triage):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 24 hours of your report (we can provide an initial summary of what we see).
- Confirmed incident notification: we follow our DPA language (notification "as required by applicable law"), but operationally we will aim to provide a consolidated incident brief within 72 hours if the event appears to involve customer personal data.
- Evidence preservation: we will initiate a 14-day preservation hold on relevant logs/containers by default; if Finex requests, we will extend preservation to support forensic work.

Subprocessors: Ben, can you prepare a short list of active subprocessors who could touch integration logs or backups and note cross-border status.

For evidence exchange we prefer an encrypted S3 pre-signed URL with limited TTL or a secure shared Drive folder with eDiscovery controls. If Finex needs forensic container access, we can provide a sanitized container snapshot via our secure share under an NDA-addendum.

I'm attaching our internal triage checklist so Ops can start collecting the relevant items. Laura — we need contractual guidance on whether the 72-hour consolidated brief should be a formal "notification" under our DPA or merely an operational update.

Next step: Ben/Marissa to confirm subprocessors and retention windows within 4 business hours. Laura to propose DPA amendment language in 24 hours if needed. Markus

Attachment: redwood_internal_triage_checklist.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T12:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence access

Markus / team,

I pulled the active subprocessors list for the Finex integration. Short summary:
- Log routing and short-term log storage: LogStream Inc. (US); no EU processing by default but backups may be replicated to eu-log-archive for compliance customers.
- Metrics aggregation: Metricly (US-hosted, no PII by design).
- Container registry/image scan: SecureImage (global, images stored in eu-west-1 when customer requests EU-only).

Immediate operational constraints:
- We can produce application-level logs for the integration within 48 hours; low-level host forensic logs may require a warrant/subpoena if they contain host-level identifiers tied to third parties.
- Cross-border movement: backup replication to eu-log-archive is opt-in per customer; I'll flag Finex's account metadata. If Finex asserts EU-residency for the affected records, we will enable EU-only retention for those log artifacts where available.

I'll stage the candidate artifacts in a locked bucket and share a pre-signed URL to Finex's security address (or to the secure Drive link they provide). ETA for list + staged artifacts: 6 hours.

Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Finex Security <security@finex.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence access

Hi all — quick legal position and proposed contract language (redline attached). Key points:

- DPA interpretation: Our current DPA ties formal "notification" obligations to events that meet the statutory definition of a personal data breach under applicable law. Operational updates (triage reports, evidence summaries) do not automatically constitute a formal notification unless they change the legal assessment. To avoid confusion we recommend issuing two deliverables: (1) an "Operational Incident Brief" within 72 hours; (2) a "Formal Notification" only if the legal threshold is met.

- Subprocessor visibility: we confirm obligation to maintain and provide an up-to-date subprocessors list on request. For expedited handoffs we can provide the list within 24 hours and prioritize relevant artifacts from those subprocessors.

- Evidence access / forensics: contractually we need an amendment that permits time-limited forensic access under an agreed NDA addendum and sets a process for cross-border transfer approvals. Attached is a proposed redline that adds: (a) a 72-hour operational brief commitment; (b) a clause allowing expedited evidence transfer under an executed access addendum; (c) a clause requiring customer confirmation if EU-restricted data is in scope before we replicate any artifacts out of the EU.

I'll upload a redline and a DocuSign envelope for the access addendum. For now please proceed with staging artifacts as Ben suggested but do not permit host-level forensic exports without a signed addendum.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: dpa_amendment_redline_v1.docx

From: Finex Security <security@finex.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence access

Laura / Markus — thanks for the rapid coordination and for the clarity on two-tiered deliverables. We accept the proposed approach: please proceed with a 72-hour Operational Incident Brief (we'll expect the deliverable by EOD 2027-04-13) and hold any host-level exports until the access addendum is signed.

Action items we are placing on Finex + Redwood: 
- Finex will provide a narrow scope list of affected customer IDs by 2027-04-11T20:00Z.
- Redwood to share the subprocessors snapshot and staged artifact pre-signed URL by 2027-04-11T20:00Z.
- Laura to send DocuSign link for the access addendum — we will aim to sign within 48 hours.

Please confirm the S3 pre-signed URL approach and that the staged bucket will be encrypted and TTL-limited. Once we have the Operational Brief we'll determine whether a Formal Notification is required under applicable law and will let you know.

Regards,
Aishwarya Patel
Head of Security Operations, Finex Technologies
security@finex.com
